# fix(upflow): name what git actually said when identity derivation fails

<!-- Generated by SessionEnd hook from a commit matching a journal-worthy pattern.
     Next session: review, then promote to a real journal entry OR delete. -->

**Commit**: `07ad4f071f64` — fix(upflow): name what git actually said when identity derivation fails

**Body**:

`_readOriginRemote` discarded stderr (`stdio[2] = "ignore"`), so every git
failure collapsed into one reason naming three causes: "no origin, not a git
repo, or git unavailable". The most common real cause in a container or on a
shared machine is a FOURTH the message never named — `detected dubious
ownership` (safe.directory). A maintainer hitting that was sent looking for a
missing remote they actually have.

stderr is now captured and its first line appended, truncated to 200 chars and
newline-stripped: the string reaches a logged refusal reason, and an unbounded
echo of subprocess output is a log-injection surface. It carries no remote URL
(git's ownership and not-a-repo errors name a PATH, and URL-bearing errors are
not on this failure path), but it is operator-environment text, so it is
bounded rather than trusted. Measured — a non-git directory now reports:
  "... dubious ownership, or git unavailable — git said: fatal: not a git
   repository (or any of the p..."

Purely diagnostic: `_lastGitStderr` is never an operand in any security
decision, only text appended to a refusal that had already been decided.

ALSO RECORDED, DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED — a mis-derivation in the ADO `_ssh`
form. Only `_git` is filtered, so `_ssh` is read as a NAME. Measured:
  ssh://acct@vs-ssh.visualstudio.com:22/Proj/_ssh/Repo
    -> {org: "proj", project: "_ssh", repo: "repo"}
The obvious fix is wrong and I traced it rather than shipping it: filtering
`_ssh` alongside `_git` makes the 3-segment form refuse (correct) but turns the
4-segment collection form into a DIFFERENT mis-derivation (collection read as
org). A correct parse needs to know where the org sits in the `_ssh` form —
ADO ground truth this repo cannot check. Fail-closed either way, since the
bogus component mismatches the caller's repoRef and the completion is refused.

Not guessed at on purpose: acting on an incomplete enumeration of ADO URL forms
is exactly what produced the collection-form regression recorded two commits
back. This one is left for someone with a real ADO org.

PUSHED BACK on the paired recommendation to refuse when the ADO project is
undeterminable. Verified the 2-segment `<org>.visualstudio.com/<project>/_git/
<repo>` form is the COMMON form and derives correctly; refusing it to close the
rare project-omitted ambiguity would break ordinary remotes. The ambiguity
stays documented, not enforced.

Suite 36/36; differential 0 findings, 21/21; disclosure clean; validate-emit
unchanged at the 49 pre-existing.
